q: 1. How many levels of Government shall be in the federal structure of Nepal?
explain: According to Article 56 of the Constitution of Nepal, the federal structure consists of three levels: Federal, Provincial, and Local.

q: 2. What is/are the features of Nepalese federal system? I. Separation of Powers II. Division of Powers III. Independent Judiciary IV. A Written Constitution
explain: The Nepalese federal system incorporates all four elements: a written constitution, division of powers among levels, separation of powers among organs, and an independent judiciary.

q: 3. On which principle, the Presidential Government operates?
explain: The Presidential system is strictly based on the principle of 'Separation of Powers,' where the executive branch is independent of the legislative branch.

q: 4. In which country, the parliamentary form of government was first introduced?
explain: The United Kingdom (UK) is considered the 'Mother of Parliaments' and is the origin of the Westminster model of parliamentary governance.

q: 5. Which of following is not the current governance system of Nepal, as provisioned by the constitution of Nepal?
options: Executive power rests with heads of state system
explain: In Nepal's parliamentary system, the executive power rests with the Council of Ministers, not solely with the Head of State (who is ceremonial).

q: 6. Parliamentary system of governance implies ---------
options: Power is vested with elected legislature
explain: The defining feature of a parliamentary system is that the executive (the cabinet) is formed from and remains accountable to the elected legislature.

q: 7. Which of the following statement is/are not correct regarding present governance system of Nepal?
options: Recognition of Nepal as a federal democratic republic nation
President to be elected by the constituent assembly on the basis of the political consensus
Sovereignty and state authority inherent in the Nepalese people
explain: The President is elected by an Electoral College (Federal and Provincial members), not the Constituent Assembly, which was dissolved after 2015.

q: 8. The President of Nepal is elected by --------
options: Elected members of Houses of Representatives
Members of both Houses of federal Parliament
An electoral college composed of the members of federal parliament and province assemblies
Elected members of Houses of the state legislatures.
explain: Per Article 62, the Electoral College includes members of the Federal Parliament (House of Representatives and National Assembly) and members of Provincial Assemblies.

q: 9. Which of the following is not a merit of the presidential system?
explain: In a presidential system, the executive is not directly responsible to the legislature, so parliamentary surveillance is significantly lower than in a parliamentary system.

q: 10. Which one is not the merit of presidential Governance system?
options: political Stability is its greater virtue
head of the state is directly accountable to people
legislature parliament is free from government making process
excessive authority in executive can make the executive authoritarian
explain: The risk of executive authoritarianism is considered a 'demerit' or disadvantage of the presidential system.

q: 11. The benefits of federal system include --------
options: Citizens that may find it easier to participate in the policy-making process working with the Central government
Central governments that may be more sensitive to the needs and desire of people.
Less populated and remote areas of the country that can find a voice in their own provincial government
explain: Federalism brings the government closer to the people, allowing remote and diverse populations to have localized representation and a voice in governance.

q: 12. Which of following is/are the current governance system of Nepal, as provisioned by the constitution of Nepal?
explain: Nepal's 2015 Constitution defines the state as a federal, democratic, republican nation with a multi-tier governance structure.

q: 13. Which is not demerit of unitary governance system?
options: Excessive dependence of people to the centre
Huge work load to central level
Poor utilization and mobilization of local resources
Coordination and cooperation among governments bodies is easier
explain: Ease of coordination is an 'advantage' (merit) of a unitary system, as there is a single centralized chain of command.

q: 14. The most essential feature of the Parliamentary form of Government is the --------
options: Accountability of the executive to the legislature
explain: The collective responsibility and accountability of the executive branch to the legislature is the core pillar of parliamentary systems.

q: 15. Who can promulgate ordinances when the parliament is not in session?
explain: Under Article 114, the President may promulgate an ordinance on the recommendation of the Council of Ministers when the Parliament is in recess.

q: 16. The benefits of the unitary system include --------
options: Government that can more easily be held accountable by its citizens
Government that can more easily promote national unity
Citizenry that can expect the same level of government services in all regions
explain: Unitary systems benefit from uniformity in laws, services, and a stronger central capacity to promote national cohesion.

q: 17. Which one of the following is a drawback of the presidential system?
options: Dictatorship of the council of ministers
In functionability of the exact separation of power
explain: A major criticism/drawback of the presidential system is that concentrated executive power can lead to authoritarian tendencies.

q: 18. Which one of the following is a characteristic of presidential system?
options: Powerful council of ministers to the legislature
explain: In many presidential systems (like the USA), the constitution remains the supreme law of the land, governing the separation of powers.

q: 19. Parliamentary form of government is run by ---------
explain: The Cabinet, or Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister, holds the actual executive power in a parliamentary system.

q: 20. Federal Legislature in Nepal is ---------
explain: The Federal Parliament of Nepal is bicameral, consisting of the House of Representatives and the National Assembly.

q: 21. The system of government in which there is only one level of government is known as ----
explain: A unitary system concentrates power in a single central government level, unlike federal systems that share power.

q: 22. What are the main objectives of a federal system?
options: To safeguard and promote unity of the country
explain: Federalism aims to balance national unity with the recognition and empowerment of regional/cultural diversity.

q: 23. Which one is not the demerit of Parliamentary Governance System?
options: Political instability is more as compared to presidential system
Head of the Government and Council of Minister are accountable to the parliament
Government with majority in legislature parliament violates the principle of separation of power
Legislature becomes engaged in government making business which constrains its business of law making
explain: Executive accountability to the parliament is considered a 'merit' (advantage), not a demerit, as it ensures democratic oversight.

q: 24. Match List I and List II and select the correct answer using the code given below...
explain: Presidential = Separation of power; Unitary = Centralization; Parliamentary = Close relationship (Exec/Leg); Federal = Division of power.

q: 25. In which article of the Constitution of Nepal has three levels of structures of state been provisioned?
explain: Article 56 of the Constitution of Nepal (2015) explicitly defines the Federal, Provincial, and Local levels of the state.

q: 26. Which part of our constitution envisages a three tier system of governance?
explain: Part 5 of the Constitution covers the 'Structure of State and Distribution of State Power,' detailing the three-tier system.

q: 27. How many national level political parties are there in Nepal at present?
explain: Based on the 2079 election results and the threshold criteria, 7 parties initially qualified as national parties in Nepal.

q: 28. Which of the following entity is responsible for settlement of political disputes arising between the federation and states?
explain: According to Article 234, the Inter-State Council is established to settle political disputes between the Federation and Provinces.

q: 29. If the President wants to resign, he/she shall address his letter of resignation to -------
explain: Per Article 67, the President submits their resignation letter to the Vice-President of Nepal.

q: 30. How many districts are there where one Representative is elected from each district?
explain: Out of 77 districts, 35 districts are delineated such that they consist of only one electoral constituency for the House of Representatives.

q: 31. How many votes were in favor and against the proposal to declare Nepal a Federal Democratic Republic in 2065 B.S.?
explain: On Jestha 15, 2065, the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly voted 559 in favor and 5 against the republic proposal.

q: 32. According to the Constitution of Nepal, one should be ____ years of age to become a candidate for the President of Nepal?
explain: Article 64 specifies that a person must have attained at least 45 years of age to be eligible for the office of President.

q: 33. What is the minimum age laid down for a candidate to seek election to the House of Representative?
explain: Article 87 states that a citizen must be at least 25 years old to be eligible for election to the House of Representatives.

q: 34. How many members are there in House of Representative in Nepal?
explain: The House of Representatives consists of 275 members (165 from FPTP and 110 from Proportional Representation).

q: 35. According to the Constitution of Nepal, what is the provision of minimum age criteria to be of the National Assembly at the time of nomination?
explain: Article 87 specifies that the minimum age for a member of the National Assembly is 35 years.

q: 36. How many members are there in the National Assembly in Nepal?
explain: The National Assembly is a 59-member permanent house (56 elected from provinces and 3 nominated by the President).

q: 37. How many members are nominated to the National Assembly by the President?
explain: Per Article 86, the President nominates three members to the National Assembly on the recommendation of the Government.

q: 38. The term of office of one third of the members of the National Assembly expire in -------
explain: The National Assembly is a permanent house where 1/3 of the members' terms expire every two years via lottery.

q: 39. In which part of the Constitution of Nepal 2072 is the Provincial Executive provisioned?
explain: Part 13 of the Constitution of Nepal (2015) contains the provisions related to the Provincial Executive.

q: 40. If a political dispute arises between a province and a municipality/rural municipality, who is responsible for resolving it?
explain: Provincial Assemblies often hold the jurisdiction and legislative oversight regarding coordination and dispute issues at the local level within the province.

q: 41. According to the Constitution of Nepal, what is the total number of Provincial Assembly members elected directly across all provinces?
explain: Across all 7 provinces, there are a total of 330 seats (twice the federal FPTP seats) elected through the FPTP system.

q: 42. Who are the members of the Inter-Provincial Council as provisioned by Nepal's Constitution?
explain: Article 234 specifies the PM (Chair), Home Minister, Finance Minister, and Chief Ministers of the provinces as members.

q: 43. According to present Constitution of Nepal, what percentage of total members of state Assembly to be elected through the first-past-the-post electoral system?
explain: The Provincial Assembly follows a 60:40 ratio: 60% elected through FPTP and 40% through Proportional Representation.

q: 44. What is the term of a Member of the Provincial assembly?
explain: The term of office for a member of the Provincial Assembly is five years unless dissolved earlier.

q: 45. How many members are there in the Provincial Assembly in Nepal?
explain: The combined total of all seven provincial assembly members in Nepal is 550 (330 FPTP + 220 PR).

q: 46. Council of ministers in provinces should not be more than ____ of total members of the provincial parliament.
explain: Article 168(9) states the Provincial Council of Ministers shall not exceed 20% of the total number of members of that Provincial Assembly.

q: 47. _______ shall appoint one Chief of Province for each province.
explain: Article 163 mandates the President to appoint a Provincial Head (Province Chief) as a representative of the Federal Government.

q: 48. According to constitution of Nepal, there will be ____ member judicial committee formed at local level in the Coordination of Vice -Chair/Deputy Mayor.
explain: Article 217 provides for a 3-member judicial committee coordinated by the Vice-Chairperson or Deputy Mayor.

q: 49. How many assemblies are there under the local level?
explain: The local level includes two types of assemblies: Village Assemblies (Gaun Sabha) and Municipal Assemblies (Nagar Sabha).

q: 50. Who of the following is not included in the Inter Province Commission which works for the solution of Generated Political Controversy...?
explain: The Chief Justice is part of the Judiciary, while the Inter-State Council is a political/administrative body headed by the Prime Minister.

q: 51. The Constitution of Nepal defines the relationship among the federation, province, and local levels based on the principle of ---------
explain: Article 232 of the Constitution states that the relationship between the three levels of government shall be based on the principles of cooperation, coexistence, and coordination.

q: 52. How many constitution bodies have been provisioned in the current Constitution of Nepal?
explain: The 2015 Constitution of Nepal provisions 13 constitutional bodies, including the CIAA, Auditor General, and various commissions for inclusion (Tharu, Muslim, etc.).

q: 53. Who appoints the chairperson and members of the Public Service Commission?
options: By president, upon the recommendation of the Constitutional Council
By president, upon the recommendation of the Government of Nepal
By president, upon the recommendation of the prime minister
By president, upon the recommendation of the Chief justice
explain: According to Article 242, the President appoints the Chairperson and members of the PSC based on the recommendation of the Constitutional Council.

q: 54. All the following includes constitutional bodies except;
options: Commission for the Investigation of abuse of authority
explain: The Office of the Comptroller General is a government department under the Ministry of Finance, not an independent constitutional body.

q: 55. How many election commissioners should be in Election Commission apart from Chief Commissioner?
explain: Article 245 states the Election Commission consists of a Chief Election Commissioner and four other Commissioners.

q: 56. How many chairperson and members are there in National Human Right Commission?
explain: As per Article 248, the NHRC consists of a Chairperson and four other members appointed from among persons with significant contributions to human rights.

q: 57. Who Chairs the Constitutional Council of Nepal?
explain: Article 284 establishes the Constitutional Council with the Prime Minister as the Chairperson.

q: 58. What is the term of office of the chairperson of Public Service Commission?
explain: The term of office for the Chairperson and members of the PSC is six years from the date of appointment.

q: 59. For the appointment of which position parliamentary hearing process is not required?
options: Vice Chairman of National Planning Commission
explain: While Constitutional body heads, Justices, and Ambassadors require parliamentary hearings (Article 292), the Vice Chair of the NPC is an executive appointment and does not.

q: 60. Under which part of Nepal's Constitution is the Public Service Commission provisioned?
explain: Part 23 of the Constitution of Nepal (2015) is dedicated to the Public Service Commission.

q: 61. Under which article of Nepal's Constitution are the functions, duties, and powers of the Public Service Commission mentioned?
explain: Article 243 details the functions, duties, and powers of the PSC, primarily focusing on conducting examinations for civil service positions.

q: 62. What is the minimum age requirement for the Chairperson of the National Human Rights Commission in Nepal as per the Constitution?
explain: Article 248(5) specifies that to be appointed as Chairperson or a member of the NHRC, one must have completed 45 years of age.

q: 63. What is the maximum age limit for the Chairperson or members of the Election Commission?
explain: According to Article 245, the office of the Chief Election Commissioner or Commissioner becomes vacant once they attain the age of 65.

q: 64. For which constitutional body's official is a master's degree from a recognized university mandatory?
options: Commission for the Investigation of Abuse of Authority
explain: Article 242(5) requires a Master's degree from a recognized university for the Chairperson and members of the PSC.

q: 65. Election Commission is a/an.....
explain: The Election Commission is established under the Constitution of Nepal, making it a permanent constitutional body.

q: 66. The declaration of constitutional emergency in Nepalese State has to be approved by the Parliament within a period of -----
explain: According to Article 273, a proclamation of emergency must be laid before the Federal Parliament for approval within one month.

q: 67. According to constitution of Nepal, the president appoints the Attorney General of Nepal on the recommendation of -------
explain: The Attorney General is appointed by the President on the specific recommendation of the Prime Minister (Article 157).

q: 68. Which of the following constitutional body cannot be monitored, evaluated, or directed by the House of Representatives?
explain: While most bodies are accountable to parliament, the NHRC's independence is emphasized internationally; however, in Nepal, they all submit reports. The NHRC specifically deals with non-derogable rights.

q: 69. Which body recommends the appointment of the heads of constitutional bodies in Nepal?
explain: The Constitutional Council is the specialized body tasked with recommending names for heads and members of constitutional commissions to the President.

q: 70. According to Constitution of Nepal, on what principle should constitutional bodies and ambassadors be appointed?
explain: Article 283 and Article 282 emphasize that appointments to constitutional bodies and ambassadors shall be made on the principle of inclusion.

q: 71. Who serves as the member-secretary of the Constitutional Council?
explain: Article 284(4) designates the Chief Secretary of the Government of Nepal to function as the Secretary of the Constitutional Council.

q: 72. To whom does the Constitutional Council submit its annual report?
explain: Annual reports of constitutional bodies are generally submitted to the President, who then causes them to be laid before the Federal Parliament.

q: 73. In the context of Nepal, which one of the following statement is not true?
options: There is a Governor as the executive head of the province
The president appoints the prime Minister
The prime Minister is responsible to the parliament
Should not be less than 25 years of age for member of House of Representatives
explain: While the President formally appoints the PM, the PM is specifically the leader who commands a majority in the House of Representatives; the 'untruth' often lies in technical wording of administrative versus executive roles in various MCQ banks.

q: 74. According to Constitution of Nepal, who among the following is not a member of the Constitutional Council?
options: Leader of the Opposition in the House of Representatives
explain: The Council includes the PM, CJ, Speaker, Chair of National Assembly, Leader of Opposition, and Deputy Speaker. The Law Minister is only a member for CJ appointments.

q: 75. According to Constitution of Nepal, to whom are the heads and officials of constitutional bodies accountable?
explain: Constitutional bodies are independent but remain accountable to the Federal Parliament, where their annual reports are discussed and evaluated.

q: 76. Following positions are there in Nepal's protocol. Choose the correct order of precedence: I. Asst. Cabinet Minister, II. Judge of Supreme Court, III. Chairperson of PSC, IV. Chief Secretary
explain: In Nepal's official protocol (order of precedence), Supreme Court Judges and the PSC Chairperson rank above Assistant Ministers and the Chief Secretary.

q: 77. What is the Ranking of speaker of House of Representatives of Nepal in the official protocol of Nepal?
explain: In the order of precedence: 1. President, 2. VP, 3. PM, 4. CJ, 5. Speaker of HoR & Chairman of National Assembly.

q: 78. As per Protocol, who among the following ranks highest in the order of precedence?
options: Governor of a State within his province
explain: The Speaker of the House of Representatives ranks 5th, which is higher than a Deputy PM or State Governor in the general hierarchy.

q: 79. When did the publication of Gazette begin in Nepal?
explain: The Nepal Gazette (Nepal Rajpatra) first began its official publication on Shrawan 22, 2008 B.S.

q: 80. How many parts were there in 'Nepal Gazette'?
explain: The Nepal Gazette is organized into 6 distinct parts, each categorizing different types of government notices, acts, and rules.
